facts.text: It was the site of a shipyard that was a major producer of the Galactic Empire's starships.

evidence.quote: It was the site of a shipyard that was a major producer of the Galactic Empire's starships.

facts.text: General Crix Madine considered the shipyard a potential target for a rebel campaign if another campaign, Operation Ringbreaker, was successful.

facts.text: During the time of the Galactic Empire, Allanteen VI was the site of a shipyard that became a major production source of Imperial starships.

evidence.quote: During the time of the Galactic Empire, Allanteen VI was the site of a shipyard that became a major production source of Imperial starships.

facts.text: General Airen Cracken of the then-unofficial Rebellion's Intelligence branch had a number of agents operating around Allanteen and other Imperial shipyard hubs including Corellia, Fondor, Kuat, and Ringo Vinda.

evidence.quote: General Airen Cracken of the then-unofficial Rebellion's Intelligence branch had a number of agents operating around Allanteen and other Imperial shipyard hubs including Corellia, Fondor, Kuat, and Ringo Vinda.

facts.text: Through those agents, he gathered information on the Imperial Navy's Star Destroyers and patrol vessels and detailed them in an official document addressed to the Rebellion's leader, Mon Mothma, that cited Allanteen VI as part of the investigations.

evidence.quote: Through those agents, he gathered information on the Imperial Navy's Star Destroyers and patrol vessels and detailed them in an official document addressed to the Rebellion's leader, Mon Mothma, that cited Allanteen VI as part of the investigations.

evidence.quote: In the current Star Wars canon, Allanteen VI was first mentioned on a map included in the fifty-second issue of De Agostini's magazine series Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon, published around December 30, 2015.

facts.text: The map only used the shorter designation "Allanteen," which was first described as a celestial body in "Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of Rogue One?," a StarWars.com article written by Mark Newbold and published on January 31 2017.
entities: Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of Rogue One?

evidence.quote: The map only used the shorter designation "Allanteen," which was first described as a celestial body in "Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of Rogue One?," a StarWars.com article written by Mark Newbold and published on January 31 2017.

facts.text: The celestial body was then given its full name in the reference book and boxed set Star Wars: The Rebel Files, written by Daniel Wallace and released on November 21 of that same year.

evidence.quote: The celestial body was then given its full name in the reference book and boxed set Star Wars: The Rebel Files, written by Daniel Wallace and released on November 21 of that same year.
